_comment: Confusable-character folding and the distance thresholds for typosquat detection
Folding runs on the ORIGINAL host string, never the normalized one. NFKC normalization
already collapses some of these, which is exactly why the analyzer must not use its
output: if `ѕbi.com` has silently become `sbi.com` by the time the URL analyzer sees it,
the homograph is invisible and the message looks clean.
Order of operations in §3.3: single-character folds first, then sequence folds, then
re-run typosquat matching against banks.json. A fold that turns an unknown host into a
known brand is a strong hit.
Note what is deliberately NOT here: leetspeak digit-to-letter folds (0->o, 1->i, 3->e).
design.md §3.2 already strips digits in the `squash` rule, so sbi1-verify.xyz is caught
there. Folding digits to letters as well would make unrelated domains collide with brand
labels in both directions and is pure false-positive surface.
Every key in `single_char_folds` must be exactly one character; the build script enforces
it. Commentary lives in this array, not interleaved with the data, so that the loader can
read the map without having to filter out pseudo-entries.
_sequence_folds_comment: Render-level confusions: sequences that look like one glyph at SMS font sizes.
Applied after single-character folding. Kept short — each entry is a chance to fold two
innocent letters into a brand match, so only the ones that genuinely deceive are listed.
_distance_comment: Damerau-Levenshtein thresholds from design.md §3.2, compared on the label with the TLD
stripped. Short brand labels get a tighter budget because at distance 2 a 3-letter label
is barely constrained: `sbi` within 2 edits reaches most three-letter strings, and the
analyzer would start flagging unrelated small businesses.
_suspicious_tlds_comment: High-abuse TLDs, yielding SUSPICIOUS_TLD at WARN (design.md §3.4). Never CRITICAL on its
own — plenty of legitimate Indian small businesses sit on .xyz because it is cheap.
Mainstream TLDs that appear on abuse lists are deliberately excluded: .info, .online,
.site, .store, .shop, .space, .live, .biz. Indian small businesses and genuine services
use all of them, and every one added here costs precision on the hard negatives that
Phase 1 must pass with zero tolerance.
